chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who commits a major sin from the major sins and then dies. Does that exit him from Islam? And if he is punished, is his punishment like the punishment of the polytheists, or does he have a period and an end? He said: 'The one who commits a major sin from the major sins and alleges that it is permissible, that exits him from Islam and he is punished with the severest punishment. And if he was acknowledging that he sinned and died upon it, that exits him from faith (Iman) and does not exit him from Islam, and his punishment is lighter than the punishment of the first one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a major sinner who is removed from Islam versus one who is only removed from faith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'intermediate status' (manzila bayn al-manzilatayn) by distinguishing between major sins committed with conviction of permissibility versus those committed with acknowledgment of fault. It establishes that while such a sinner remains within the fold of Islam, their faith is diminished, leading to a punishment distinct from that of polytheists. This distinction underscores the Shia view that major sins do not necessarily equate to apostasy unless accompanied by a denial of their prohibition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man committing the major sin from the major sins, and he dies. Would that exit him from Al-Islam? And if he was Punished, would his Punishment be like the Punishment of the Polytheists, or would there be a time limit for him and a cutting off?’ So heasws said: ‘The one who commits a major sin from the major sins, and he alleges that it is Permissible, that would exit him from Al Islam and he would be Punished with the severest of the Punishments; and if he was acknowledging that he is sinning, and he dies upon it, that would exit him from the Emān and it would not exit him from Al-Islam, and his Punishment would be lesser than the Punishment of the first one’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about a man who commits a major sin and then dies whether it takes him away from Islam and if he will be punished, will it be like that for the pagans or will it finish on a certain time? The Imam said, ‘One who commits any of the major sins considering it to be lawful it will take him away from Islam and he will face the most severe punishment. However, if he affirms that what he has done is a sin and dies, he is taken out of belief but not out of Islam and his punishment will be less severe than the one mentioned before.’”
